title: observability: add token-level KV/cache cost & latency dashboard panels + alert tuning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We need better visibility into per-token economics and KV cache behavior so oncall and SRE teams can detect regressions in latency and cost quickly. This PR adds new Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry span attributes, Grafana dashboard panels for token-level cost/latency and KV cache hit/miss breakdowns, and refines alert thresholds based on observed 90/95/99 latency distributions.

Summary of changes: 1) New metrics: redwood_tokens_cost_total (counter, per-model, per-route), redwood_tokens_latency_seconds_bucket (histogram by token type request/response), redwood_kv_cache_hits_total and redwood_kv_cache_misses_total (counters, per-model, shard). 2) Tracing: add token_count and kv_cache_hit boolean attributes to inference spans; standardize span names to inference.{model}.{route} for easier filtering. 3) Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard `Token-level Cost & KV Cache` with panels for token cost breakdown (prompt vs completion), per-token latency heatmap, KV hit ratio time series, KV cost per-token. 4) Alerts: tuned alert rules for token p95/p99 tail latency, sudden drop in KV hit ratio (>10% drop sustained 5m), and token cost spikes (>2x baseline for 3m). 5) Docs: updated observability playbook and dashboard README with guidance and runbook links. 6) Tests: unit tests for metrics exposition and an integration smoke test in perf-canary that validates metrics flow.

Checklist:
- [x] Add new Prometheus metrics and exposition code
- [x] Add span attributes and update tracing docs
- [x] Create Grafana dashboard JSON + screenshots
- [x] Add/adjust alerting rules and thresholds
- [x] Add unit & integration tests
- [x] Update observability playbook and alert runbooks

Context/Notes: We sampled production traffic in the `canary` workspace for 72 hours to calibrate thresholds (see linked Linear tasks). The KV hit ratio tends to float between 65-85% depending on workload; alerts use a 10% relative drop guardrail to avoid noisy alerts on workload variance. Token cost is computed from model unit cost multiplied by emitted tokens; there is a small smoothing window (30s) applied in dashboards to avoid 1s jitter spikes.

Related: previous dashboards and alert tuning work in ENG-3189 and ENG-3342. This PR focuses on token/KV-level observability; additional routing-level panels will be added in follow-ups.

Merge: squash and merge after CI green and two approvals.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Please ensure the prometheus metric names follow our naming conventions (no pluralization) and include unit labels. Also suggest adding a per-route label to kv_cache_* metrics for easier query scoping.

Maya Chen: Addressed in token_metrics.go — renamed tokens_cost_total -> redwood_tokens_cost_total and added route,label model labels. kv metrics now include route label. Updated docs to call out units and example queries.
Priya Natarajan: The p99 alert looks tight for busy routes — can we use an adaptive baseline computed from a 7d rolling median?
Maya Chen: We decided to use a static relative threshold with a cooldown to avoid complexity; added a comment and runbook note explaining follow-up work to evaluate adaptive baselining (ENG-3498).
Samir Patel: CI failed on first run due to a flaky test in token_metrics_test.go referencing time.Now() directly — suggest switching to clock injection.
Maya Chen: Switched tests to use testclock and fixed flaky assertion. Re-ran CI and all checks passed.

release_notes: Add token-level cost and latency metrics + KV cache hit/miss metrics, new Grafana dashboard 'Token-level Cost & KV Cache', and tuned alerts for token p95/p99 and KV hit ratio drops. Improves observability for oncall and cost monitoring.
notes_for_oncall: New alerts added: token_latency_p95_spike, token_latency_p99_spike, kv_hit_ratio_drop. See observability/alerts/*.yaml and the playbook for runbook steps. If KV hit ratio drops, check recent model/prefix changes and cache eviction logs; fallback is configured to route to lower-latency model variants if sustained.
author_response_summary: Fixed metric naming, added route labels, switched tests to testclock, documented threshold rationale and follow-up work ENG-3498.
notes: Dashboard JSON is included and will be synced by scripts/dashboard-sync.sh during release. Helm values default to disabled for high-cardinality token metrics; enable via values-observability.yaml if needed for specific deployments.
